summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and coronary artery disease was admitted for chest pressure, hypertension, and generalized weakness. His symptoms began over the weekend with elevated blood pressure and headache, which partially improved with rest. He presented to his primary care provider with new-onset chest pressure, nausea, and reduced oral intake. Evaluation revealed no acute cardiac ischemia, with normal EKG and undetectable troponin. A chest X-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. He was treated with IV fluids, leading to resolution of chest pressure and improvement in orthostatic symptoms. His outpatient cardiologist, neurologist, and mitochondrial specialist were consulted; no new therapies were recommended due to his initial hypertension. Outpatient IV hydration was arranged closer to his home. He was discharged asymptomatic with continued management focused on hydration and monitoring.
